features.name: Academic credential level
features.description: Captures the level of formal academic preparation or degree attainment the applicant presents as relevant to the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree, equivalent, or no advanced degree is presented.
Master's degree is presented.
Doctoral degree is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct experience designing agent-based systems, especially architectures, guardrails, supervision, permissions, and bounded autonomy.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter provides concrete evidence of practical skill with data structures and algorithms in real engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has actually shipped AI or LLM functionality in production and treats reliability, evaluation, or controls as part of that work.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Collaboration posture
features.description: Captures readiness to partner constructively with security specialists and other internal stakeholders, including humility and service orientation in collaborative work.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant frames security engineering as a constructive, developer-centered practice built around secure defaults, usability, empathy, and prevention rather than policing.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how much the letter substantiates its claims with concrete mechanisms, named systems, examples, or other specific details rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's real production backend work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter states the concrete outcomes or effects of the applicant's work, not just the activities performed.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: Captures the range of programming languages the applicant presents beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: Shows narrow breadth beyond the main language or two.
Shows moderate breadth across several additional languages.
Shows very broad breadth across many additional languages.

features.name: Narrative cohesion
features.description: Captures whether the letter forms a coherent professional story or career arc rather than a disconnected checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Captures how memorable and individually voiced the letter feels, including whether its opening or framing stands out in a role-relevant way.

levels.descriptor: The letter feels interchangeable, checklist-driven, or heavily templated.
The letter has some personal framing, but is still mostly standard and forgettable.
The letter has a noticeable voice or framing device that helps the applicant stand out.
The letter delivers a vivid, controlled narrative that is both memorable and well matched to the role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside ordinary product work, especially through CTFs or similar adversarial exercises.

levels.descriptor: No adversarial practice outside normal work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional participation or casual practice without depth signals.
The letter shows regular or serious engagement in adversarial exercises.
The letter shows unusually strong external practice, such as near-top finishes or another high-commitment signal.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures the degree of responsibility the applicant shows in public software ecosystems, from upstream fixes to maintainership and releases.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures how technically ambitious, substantial, and self-directed the applicant's personal or side projects appear.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
The project mentioned is small and mainly serves as lightweight practice or curiosity.
The project shows substantial self-directed engineering with meaningful system design or operational concerns.
The project is an ambitious systems build that tackles hard distributed-systems, storage, or reliability problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for building foundational infrastructure or shared tooling whose benefits compound across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production delivery breadth
features.description: Captures the breadth of real production-system ownership and lifecycle responsibility the applicant claims across launches, maintenance, testing, and operated services.

levels.descriptor: Production scope is vague or very limited, with at most one clearly owned service.
The letter shows clear responsibility across about 2 production services.
The letter shows repeated production delivery across about 4 services.
The letter shows broad production breadth across 6 or more services or similarly wide operational scope.

features.name: Production software track record
features.description: Captures overall depth of hands-on production software experience, especially maintaining, testing, operating, and launching real systems, often combining both duration and scope.

levels.descriptor: The letter gives thin or barely qualifying evidence of production software experience.
The letter shows solid early-career production experience with at least some testing, maintenance, or launch responsibility.
The letter shows multiple years of work and several production systems launched or maintained.
The letter shows extensive experience well beyond the minimums, with repeated launches and sustained ownership of production systems.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how concretely and substantially the letter shows Python as a real production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only minimally mentioned.
Python is mentioned for light scripting or general familiarity.
Python is used regularly for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
Python is presented as production-grade and central, with evidence of robust service or tooling development.

features.name: Relevant software tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience the letter claims, measured mainly by duration or years worked.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Reliability and maintainer mindset
features.description: Captures emphasis on maintainability, rigor, correctness, failure awareness, and long-term operability in security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Role-specific fit and motivation
features.description: Captures how specifically and convincingly the letter explains fit for this exact role by linking the applicant's motivation, background, and experience to the team's mission and responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures direct experience reviewing systems for security issues through methods like threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, and remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures whether the letter understands the role as multiplying security capacity through automation, triage, agents, or other systems that scale scarce security expertise.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents formal external security credentials and how rigorous or practice-oriented they appear.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures hands-on experience automating the intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or other workflow handling of vulnerability reports.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general automation interest, but not with a concrete vulnerability triage example.
Describes a clear example of automating vulnerability intake or routing.
Describes a strong triage automation example with several functions such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, routing, or measurable manual-load reduction.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the surface-level mechanical quality of the letter, including spelling, grammar, proofreading, and copy-editing care.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.
